headline: Artificial intelligence sharpened both sides of the ledger, as the UAT-10147 crew automated web-server attacks while enterprises doubled hiring for AI skills and wrestled with unvetted tools.

emerging_trends.text: Both attackers and defenders lean harder on automation, as enterprises double their hunt for AI skills even while a handful of super-adopters hardcode unvetted tools into critical systems.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI Reshapes Security Work and Risk

emerging_trends.text: Financial-sector fraud runs on ever-cheaper infrastructure, with Chameleon SEO Poisoning cloaking fake bank pages that evade scanners while breaches ripple through firms like Apollo Global.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Chameleon SEO Poisoning Fake Bank Sites

emerging_trends.text: Malware keeps colonizing hardware no one monitors, as Kaspersky documents the first car head-unit infection enrolling SIM-equipped dashboards into a proxy botnet.

topics.title: Breaches at Apollo Global, ReliaQuest, and a Korean Startup Platform
topics.latest_developments: Private equity firm Apollo Global disclosed a breach exposing personal information within a campaign targeting major financial companies; ReliaQuest confirmed hackers impersonated its own security team to social-engineer an employee after a ShinyHunters intrusion, though the data-theft attempt failed; and South Korea's government-backed startup platform leaked encrypted personal data after developers embedded the encryption key in an API.
topics.summary: The incidents span a private equity giant, a security vendor, and a public startup platform, exposing social-engineering and key-management failures. Organizations should rotate keys, keep them separate from the data they protect, and drill staff against impersonation.

sources.title: Personal Information Exposed in Apollo Global Data Breach
ReliaQuest confirms failed data-theft attack after ShinyHunters breach
South Korean startup platform breach exposes key management failures

topics.title: AI Reshapes Security Work and Risk
topics.latest_developments: Akamai found the top 5% of enterprise AI power users hardcode unvetted tools into critical operations; the Cisco-founded AI Workforce Consortium reported cybersecurity job ads demanding AI skills doubled to 28.5% across G7 markets in a year; and Anthropic widened Mythos 5 access for defenders through its Claude Security beta and pledged a $35 million open-source fund.
topics.summary: AI now drives hiring, tooling, and risk across security teams, with a small band of super-adopters concentrating the danger as demand for AI-fluent staff climbs and vendors push defensive scanning. Inventory shadow AI, vet embedded tools, and upskill staff.

sources.title: The Outsized Shadow: Why 5% of AI Users Are Your Biggest Security Risk
Cybersecurity job ads demanding AI skills double in a year
Anthropic Expands Mythos 5 Access to More Defenders, Unveils $35M Open Source Fund

topics.title: Android Car Head-Unit Proxy Botnet
topics.latest_developments: Kaspersky attributed the car head-unit malware to Chinese operators and called it the first documented case of malware built for that device class, spreading through the units' built-in software updaters to enroll internet-connected, SIM-equipped head units in a proxy botnet and run ad fraud.
topics.summary: Infected Android head units, many carrying SIM slots and direct internet access, join a proxy botnet and commit ad fraud through legitimate updaters. Owners and vendors should scrutinize head-unit update sources and firmware integrity.

sources.title: Hackers infecting Android car systems to build proxy botnet
Android car head units infected with proxy botnet malware through built-in software updaters

topics.title: CISA Emergency Zimbra Patch Order
topics.latest_developments: CISA ordered US federal agencies to patch an actively exploited Zimbra Collaboration Suite flaw within three days, tightening the clock on a bug already sitting in its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
topics.summary: The directive escalates pressure on the Zimbra command-injection vulnerability attackers now exploit in the wild, echoing a broader disclosure surge that pushed the Spring application framework past 200 patched flaws this year. Patch Zimbra immediately and audit Spring dependencies.

sources.title: CISA orders urgent patching of actively exploited Zimbra flaw
91 Vulnerabilities Patched in Spring Application Framework

topics.title: UAT-10147 AI-Scaled Server Attacks
topics.latest_developments: Researchers disclosed UAT-10147, a Chinese-speaking cybercrime crew that leans on AI to scale attacks against Windows and Linux web servers worldwide, dropping an implant called SPECTRE that carries EDR bypass and a Linux rootkit.
topics.summary: UAT-10147 strikes servers across education, media, technology, and gaming, concentrating on Brazil, Bolivia, China, Canada, and Vietnam, and pairs AI-assisted tooling with EDR evasion and kernel-level persistence. Harden and patch internet-facing servers and hunt for the rootkit.

sources.title: UAT-10147 Uses AI to Scale Server Attacks, Deploys SPECTRE With EDR Bypass and Linux Rootkit

topics.title: Chameleon SEO Poisoning Fake Bank Sites
topics.latest_developments: Fortra's threat intelligence unit, Fortra Intelligence and Research Experts, detailed Chameleon SEO Poisoning, a technique it tracked for three months that ranks cloaked fake banking pages for high-intent search terms and makes them play dead to dodge scanners, with cases up 40% in the second quarter of 2026.
topics.summary: Attackers poison search results for terms like a bank's login page to funnel victims to credential-harvesting clones that hide from automated scanners. Banks and users should watch for lookalike domains and verify URLs before entering credentials.

sources.title: Fake bank websites play dead to evade security scanners

business_politics.title: U.S.-Canada Trade Talks Collapse
business_politics.latest_developments: President Trump said August 24 the United States will raise tariffs on Canadian automobiles and parts to 50% starting in January, and formal U.S.-Canada negotiations broke down over the weekend without a deal.
business_politics.summary: Trade talks between Washington and Ottawa fell apart, and Trump moved to lift the U.S. tariff on Canadian cars and auto parts to 50% effective January, escalating a trade war between the two neighbors and largest trading partners and threatening cross-border supply chains for automakers.

sources.title: President Trump said Monday the U.S. will impose 50% tariffs on automobiles and parts from Canada starting in January
U.S.-Canada Trade Talks Fail
Trump says US to increase tariffs on Canadian cars to 50%

business.title: Highmark Health Earnings Rebound
business.latest_developments: Highmark Health reported August 24 that first-half earnings soared on the strength of its insurance arm, a year after the company sank more than $175 million into the red.
business.summary: Highmark Health, the Pittsburgh-based Blue Cross insurer and parent of Allegheny Health Network, swung back to strong profit in the first half of 2026, with rising second-quarter operating income driven by its insurance business and reversing last year's steep loss.

sources.title: Highmark's 1st-half earnings soar, driven by insurance arm
Highmark Health boosts Q2 operating income

business.title: Scarmazzi Homes Names Canon Theatre
business.latest_developments: The Canonsburg Educational and Cultural Institute announced August 24 that builder Scarmazzi Homes signed a 15-year deal to become founding naming sponsor of the new Canon Theatre in Canonsburg.
business.summary: Scarmazzi Homes, a Washington County homebuilder, will lend its name to the new Canon Theatre in downtown Canonsburg under a 15-year sponsorship with the Canonsburg Educational and Cultural Institute, backing the venue's opening.

sources.title: Builder invests in 15-year naming deal for new Canon Theatre

business.title: Blank Rome Builds Out Construction Practice
business.latest_developments: Blank Rome said August 24 it hired a Jones Day partner in Pittsburgh and tapped him to co-chair its firmwide construction and infrastructure practice.
business.summary: The law firm Blank Rome recruited a partner from rival Jones Day in Pittsburgh to co-lead its firmwide Construction and Infrastructure practice, deepening the firm's building-and-infrastructure bench.

sources.title: Blank Rome hires Jones Day partner to co-chair firmwide construction practice

around_town.title: Pittsburgh Public Schools Start the Year
around_town.latest_developments: Pittsburgh Public Schools opened classes August 24 with updated policies and new curriculum, and Mayor Corey O'Connor greeted students at several buildings, including Arlington PreK-8.
around_town.summary: Students across Pittsburgh Public Schools returned to classrooms Monday under revised policies and new course offerings, as the district also prepares for building closures set to take effect at the end of the school year.

sources.title: Students return to Pittsburgh Public Schools with new policies and curriculum
Pittsburgh Public Schools students head back to class

around_town.title: County to Spray Six Neighborhoods for West Nile
around_town.latest_developments: The Allegheny County Health Department said it will spray for mosquitoes in six Pittsburgh neighborhoods on Wednesday, August 26, after recent positive West Nile Virus tests.
around_town.summary: The Allegheny County Health Department scheduled mosquito spraying across six Pittsburgh neighborhoods for Wednesday following positive West Nile Virus samples, a routine effort to knock down the virus-carrying population.

sources.title: 6 Pittsburgh neighborhoods to be sprayed after positive West Nile Virus tests

around_town.title: Post-Gazette's Wischnowski to Step Down
around_town.latest_developments: The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette said August 24 that executive editor Stan Wischnowski will step down in late September.
around_town.summary: Stan Wischnowski, executive editor of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, will leave the newsroom's top job in late September, a leadership change at the region's largest daily.

sources.title: Post-Gazette editor Stan Wischnowski to step down in late September

events.title: Turkey Fund Kickoff Show at the Pittsburgh Playhouse
events.latest_developments: KDKA opened ticket sales August 24 for the 45th annual Pittsburgh Today Live Turkey Fund Kickoff Show.
events.summary: KDKA's Pittsburgh Today Live holds its 45th annual Turkey Fund Kickoff Show on Friday, September 18, 2026, at 9 a.m. at the Pittsburgh Playhouse, benefiting the Greater Pittsburgh Community Food Bank, with guests Joe Manganiello and Kaitlin O'Connor; tickets are on sale now.

sources.title: Get tickets for Pittsburgh Today Live's 45th annual Turkey Fund Kickoff Show

around_teams.title: Ramsey Returns, Porter at an Impasse
around_teams.latest_developments: Coach Mike McCarthy said August 24 that cornerback Jalen Ramsey came off the physically-unable-to-perform list to practice and rookie first-round tackle Max Iheanachor returned after 2½ weeks out, while contract talks with cornerback Joey Porter Jr. hit an impasse and Porter stayed on PUP.
around_teams.summary: The Steelers got their versatile veteran defensive back Jalen Ramsey back on the field and saw first-round pick Max Iheanachor practice again after a shoulder-and-neck injury, but McCarthy said the club and Joey Porter Jr. remain stuck on a contract extension as the fourth-year corner sits on the PUP list with a back issue.

sources.title: The Steelers get good news as Jalen Ramsey comes off the PUP list. But what about Joey Porter Jr.?

around_teams.title: Debate Over Keeping Four Quarterbacks
around_teams.latest_developments: Pittsburgh columnists argued August 22 through 24 over whether the Steelers should carry four quarterbacks into the season.
around_teams.summary: With Mason Rudolph, Will Howard, and Drew Allar competing for backup jobs behind Aaron Rodgers, TribLive's Mark Madden said keeping all four would have zero impact on the season, TribLive's Tim Benz saw value in holding onto the group, and the Post-Gazette's Noah Hiles argued rostering four passers would be a mistake.

sources.title: Noah Hiles: The Steelers would be wrong to roster four quarterbacks in 2026

team_usa.title: Rose Lavelle Leaves With Head Injury
team_usa.latest_developments: U.S. women's national team midfielder Rose Lavelle left in the first half of Gotham FC's scoreless NWSL draw with Angel City FC on Sunday, August 23, with a head injury.
team_usa.summary: Gotham FC substituted playmaker Rose Lavelle, a mainstay of the U.S. women's national team, before halftime of a 0-0 draw against Angel City FC, a worrying exit for a key American midfielder as the NWSL season continues.

sources.title: U.S. international Lavelle suffers head injury

reading.author: Cal Newport
reading.title: Has AI Gone Rogue?
reading.summary: Newport argues the real AI story of the summer is the shaky financial footing of the labs chasing record IPOs, cutting against the breathless narrative of runaway machine autonomy.

reading.author: Stratechery
reading.title: Autonomy and Innovation
reading.summary: Ben Thompson contends that in agentic cybersecurity the incentives favor offense, the same dynamic that will hamstring incumbents and give startups room to grow over the long run.

reading.author: Ed Zitron
reading.title: What Happens If OpenAI Dies?
reading.summary: Zitron games out the fallout if OpenAI collapses, arguing the company's precarious finances would ripple across the AI industry and the investors and vendors betting on it.
